title: Shrimp and Avocado Salsa in Pita Toasts
ingredients: ¾ pound bay shrimp, drained but not rinsed
¼ cup finely chopped sweet or red onion
1 ½ cups chopped ripe red tomatoes
1 ripe avocado, peeled and cut into ¼-inch dice
4 pita bread rounds, cut into 8 triangles each
method: Gently toss the shrimp, onion, tomatoes, avocado, jalapeño, lime juice, cocktail sauce and chopped cilantro together in a non-reactive bowl.
Cover and chill the salsa for 2 to 3 hours, then salt to taste.
Warm the pita triangles briefly so they heat through without turning crisp.
Open the pita pockets, fill with the shrimp salsa and arrange on a platter with cilantro sprigs.

title: Quesadillas with Smoked Mussels, Havarti, and Roasted Red Peppers
ingredients: 2 teaspoons chopped fresh dill (1 teaspoon dried)
½ cup chopped roasted red bell peppers (see page 116)
method: Heat the oven to 350°F and set 4 tortillas on a large baking sheet.
Scatter the Havarti over them, then add the mussels, dill, roasted peppers and jalapeños.
Cover each with a second tortilla.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes until the cheese melts, pressing the tops down once it starts melting so they stick together.
Cut each quesadilla into quarters and serve on a platter with dill sprigs.

title: Poached Swordfish with Champagne-Grape Sauce
ingredients: 1 teaspoon chopped fresh thyme (½ teaspoon dried)
¼ cup halved green seedless grapes
¼ cup halved red seedless grapes
2 tablespoons unsalted butter at room temperature
method: Boil the stock, sparkling wine, shallots, thyme and mustard in a large skillet over medium-high heat until reduced by half.
Add the swordfish, lower to a simmer, cover and poach 10 to 12 minutes until cooked through.
Lift out the fish and keep it warm wrapped in foil.
Turn up the heat and boil the liquid until it is thick enough to coat a spoon.
Stir in the capers and grapes for 1 to 2 minutes, then take off the heat and swirl in the butter.
Top the fish with the grapes, sauce and almonds; a squash purée makes a good side.

title: Wild Mushroom and Goat Cheese Bruschetta
ingredients: 5 ounces portobello mushrooms, inner gills removed
Kosher salt and red pepper flakes
16 thin slices of French sour baguette
GARNISH: minced lemon zest and minced chives, mixed together
method: Trim the mushrooms and chop them roughly.
Warm the oil and butter in a large skillet over medium heat; cook the garlic and shallot 1 to 2 minutes, stirring.
Turn the heat up a little, add the mushrooms and cook 7 to 8 minutes.
Pour in the sherry and stock, add thyme and basil, and cook until the liquid is gone; season and keep warm.
Heat the broiler. Spread the baguette slices with goat cheese and pile the mushrooms on top.
Broil 3 to 4 minutes until the mushrooms start to brown, then sprinkle with the lemon zest and chive mix.

title: Shrimp-Scallop Pâté with Cilantro, Dill, and Pine Nuts
ingredients: 2 tablespoons chopped fresh dill (1 tablespoon dried)
¼ teaspoon Tabasco or other hot sauce
Kosher salt and ground white pepper
GARNISH: thin slices of lemon, cilantro sprigs
method: Cook the scallops in the butter over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes.
Pulse the scallops and shrimp in a food processor until coarsely chopped; set aside.
Sprinkle the gelatin over the V-8 in a small pot, wait 7 to 8 minutes, then stir over medium heat until dissolved. Let cool.
Whisk in the herbs, lemon juice, Worcestershire, Tabasco, sour cream, pine nuts and seafood; season so it stays mild, not spicy.
Line a 2½-cup mold with plastic wrap, fill it, cover and chill at least 4 hours or overnight.
Turn out onto a plate, garnish with lemon slices and cilantro, and serve cold with crackers.

title: Roasted Eggplant-Garlic Soup
serves: 8 as an appetizer or 4 as an entrée
ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
½ cup chopped fresh basil (¼ cup dried)
1 tablespoon chopped fresh thyme (½ tablespoon dried)
GARNISH: basil sprigs, chopped red bell pepper
method: Heat the oven to 375°F. Slice the unpeeled eggplant into ¼-inch rounds, season, and drain on paper towels 20 to 30 minutes.
Cut the top off the garlic, drizzle with oil, season and wrap loosely in foil.
Roast eggplant and garlic on an oiled sheet for 15 minutes; take out the eggplant and roast the garlic 35 minutes more.
Cut the eggplant into 1-inch chunks.
Cook the onions, basil, thyme and pepper flakes in 1 tablespoon oil over medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes until soft.
Squeeze in the roasted garlic, add eggplant, tomatoes and stock, boil, then cover and simmer 10 to 12 minutes.
Purée in batches, reheat well, season and top with basil and chopped red pepper.

title: Black-eyed Pea and Tomato Soup with Cabbage
ingredients: 2 cups fresh or frozen black-eyed peas
1 large red onion, peeled and chopped (about 2 cups)
Kosher salt and red pepper flakes
GARNISH: chopped parsley, grated Parmesan cheese
method: Cover the peas and ham with cold salted water in a large pot, boil, then simmer covered 15 minutes until the peas are just tender. Drain and set aside.
Heat the oil in the same pot over medium-high heat.
Cook the garlic, onion, carrots, celery, herbs and caraway 6 to 7 minutes until the onion is translucent but the vegetables still have bite.
Add the tomatoes, V-8 and stock, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in the cabbage, peas and ham for the last 4 to 5 minutes only, so the cabbage stays crisp.
Season, ladle into bowls and top with parsley and Parmesan; serve with garlic sourdough bread.

title: Sid's Caesar
ingredients: ⅓ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
¾ tablespoon chopped roasted garlic (see page 164)
4 slices sourdough or other hearty French or Italian bread
⅛ teaspoon Tabasco or other hot sauce
1¾ pounds romaine lettuce, cut into bite-sized pieces
method: Heat the oven or toaster oven to 375°F.
Blend the anchovies, pepper, roasted garlic and olive oil 1 minute until smooth, then add the Parmesan and blend 30 seconds more.
Take out 3 tablespoons of this mixture and brush it on both sides of the bread.
Bake the bread about 20 minutes until crusty but not burnt, then break into crouton-size pieces.
Drop a cold egg into boiling water for 1 minute 15 seconds, then lift out and cool.
Whisk the remaining anchovy oil with the vinegar, lemon juice, mustard, celery salt, zest, Tabasco and Worcestershire, then scoop in the soft egg and whisk well. Chill.
Toss the cold romaine with the re-whisked dressing, add the croutons, toss again and serve on chilled plates.

title: Chilled Leeks with Green Olives, Capers, and Sun-Dried Tomato Vinaigrette
serves: 4 as an appetizer or side dish
ingredients: ⅔ cup thinly sliced sun-dried tomatoes packed in oil
¼ teaspoon black pepper or more to taste
¼ cup pitted, chopped green olives
method: Cut off the dark green leek tops, leaving a little green and the root end so each leek holds together.
Simmer the leeks, covered, in boiling salted water 10 to 12 minutes until tender, then plunge into ice water.
Hard-boil the eggs in the same water for 10 minutes, cool, chop and set aside.
Split the cooled leeks lengthwise without cutting through the root, peel off the outer layer and rinse out any grit.
Chill the leeks 2 hours (or 20 to 30 minutes in the freezer if rushed).
Mix the sun-dried tomatoes, vinegar, mustard, salt, pepper, capers and olives, then whisk in the oil slowly; season and chill.
Fan the leeks on cold plates, drizzle with the vinaigrette and scatter with chopped egg.

title: Mixed Greens with Thyme-Scented Goat Cheese Cakes and Balsamic-Dijon Vinaigrette
ingredients: 3 teaspoons chopped fresh thyme (1½ teaspoons dried)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Shape the goat cheese into 12 small patties, set in a shallow dish, top with the 2 tablespoons oil and fresh thyme, and chill 1 hour.
Mix the bread crumbs with the dried thyme, pepper and salt, and press onto both sides of each patty.
Whisk the vinegar and mustard, then slowly whisk in the ¾ cup oil and season.
Bake the cheese cakes on a sheet at 350°F for 15 minutes until golden.
Toss the greens with the vinaigrette, divide among 6 plates and top each with 2 warm cheese cakes and flowers if using.

title: Radish Slaw with Rémoulade and Pistachios
ingredients: ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
½ tablespoon chopped fresh thyme (¼ tablespoon dried)
2 tablespoons chopped cornichons or dill pickles
½ teaspoon liquid from canned chipotle chiles in adobo or hot sauce (optional)
1 large daikon radish (about 8 ounces), peeled and diced
1 bunch red radishes (about 10 radishes), stemmed and thinly sliced
method: Lower the egg into boiling water for 90 seconds to barely cook it.
Blend the egg with lemon juice, mustard, salt and pepper, then pour in the oil slowly with the motor running until thick.
Blend in the tomato paste, herbs, capers, cornichons and chipotle liquid; adjust seasoning.
Toss the daikon, red radishes and celery with about ½ cup of the rémoulade (keep the rest refrigerated up to 3 to 5 days).
Chill the slaw 2 to 3 hours.
Just before serving, mix in the pistachios, keeping a few to sprinkle on top; serve over greens if plating.

title: Roasted Potato and Carrot Salad with Basil-Citrus Dressing
serves: 6 as an appetizer or side dish
ingredients: 3 pounds small new or purple potatoes, rinsed
½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1 pound cherry tomatoes, halved (mixed red and yellow, if available)
¼ teaspoon jalapeño Tabasco or other hot sauce
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Heat the oven to 375°F. Prick the potatoes with a fork.
Toss the potatoes and whole carrots with the oil, salt and pepper in a roasting pan and roast 1 hour.
Let cool, then quarter the potatoes, cut the carrots into 1-inch pieces and combine with the tomatoes.
For the dressing, whisk the green onions, basil, citrus juices, sour cream, mustard, honey and Tabasco, then drizzle in the oil while whisking; season.
Fold the dressing through the vegetables, season, and chill covered 2 to 3 hours.
Serve at room temperature.

title: Prawn–Celery Root Salad with Ruby Grapefruit and Toasted Pine Nuts
ingredients: ⅓ cup fresh ruby grapefruit juice
½ teaspoon hot sauce (Inner Beauty brand preferred)
1 pound cooked, peeled, and deveined prawns
2 heads celery root (about 1¾ pounds), peeled and shredded
3 whole ruby grapefruit, peeled and sectioned with white membrane removed
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Whisk all the dressing ingredients together in a small non-reactive bowl.
In a larger bowl, combine the prawns, celery root, green onions, parsley, tomatoes and grapefruit segments.
Fold in the dressing, cover and chill 2 to 3 hours, then season.
Separate, wash and dry whole butter lettuce leaves and set them as cups on chilled plates.
Spoon the salad into the lettuce cups and scatter toasted pine nuts over the top.

title: Pizza with Peppered Shrimp, Canadian Bacon, Mushrooms, and Feta Cheese
ingredients: 1 cup warm tap water (110° to 115°F on an instant-read thermometer)
¼ cup plus ½ tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil
2½ tablespoons chopped mixed herbs (parsley, basil, oregano)
2½ tablespoons chopped sun-dried tomatoes packed in oil
4 teaspoons chopped fresh dill (2 teaspoons dried)
½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
¼ cup diced Canadian bacon or ham
¾ cup sliced crimini or shiitake mushrooms
¼ cup chopped roasted red peppers (see page 116)
method: Stir the warm water, sugar and yeast together and leave 8 to 10 minutes until foamy, then stir in ¼ cup of the oil.
Pulse the flour, salt and white pepper in a food processor, add the herbs and sun-dried tomatoes, then pour in the yeast mixture with the motor running until a ball forms.
Knead on a floured surface 5 to 8 minutes until smooth and springy, adding water or flour as needed.
Turn the dough in a bowl greased with the remaining ½ tablespoon oil, cover and let rise somewhere warm until doubled.
Punch down and stretch to about ½ inch thick on a 12-inch pan dusted with flour and cornmeal, leaving a thicker rim.
Whisk the tomato sauce, roasted garlic, dill, salt, ¼ teaspoon pepper and lemon juice, and spread over the dough.
Add the bacon, mushrooms, roasted peppers and feta, then the shrimp seasoned with the remaining ¼ teaspoon pepper, and sprinkle with pepper flakes.
Bake on the top rack at 450°F for 16 to 18 minutes until the crust is golden.

title: Risotto with Lemon Shrimp, Roasted Garlic, and Goat Cheese
serves: 6 as an appetizer or 4 as an entrée
ingredients: 12 ounces medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
method: Whisk the marinade ingredients, add the shrimp and refrigerate covered 1 to 2 hours.
Tip shrimp and marinade into a saucepan and cook 3 to 4 minutes until the shrimp turn pink; lift them out and keep warm.
Heat the oil and 1 tablespoon butter in a large saucepan over medium heat and cook the mushrooms and shallots 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the rice and stir 4 to 5 minutes to coat it in fat.
Pour in the wine and lemon juice carefully and simmer until almost gone.
Add the hot stock ½ cup at a time, stirring until each addition is absorbed; after 2 cups, taste and keep going until the rice is al dente.
Stir in the goat cheese, roasted garlic, zest, green onions, shrimp and remaining butter over the heat.
Serve in warm bowls ringed with the shrimp and halved cherry tomatoes.

title: Pappardelle Frutti di Mare "Mediterraneo"
serves: 6 to 8 as an appetizer or 4 as an entrée
ingredients: 1 pound mixed seafood (cleaned calamari, cut into rings, bay scallops, rock shrimp)
12 ounces fresh sea bass, cut into small pieces
½ cup fish or chicken stock
½ cup chopped sun-dried tomatoes packed in oil
½ teaspoon toasted fennel seed, crushed
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
GARNISH: freshly grated Parmesan, chopped parsley
method: Put a large pot of salted water on to boil.
Cook the shallots and garlic in the oil over medium heat 1 to 2 minutes without browning.
Add the mixed seafood and sea bass and cook 3 to 4 minutes, stirring often.
Add the wine, stock, all the tomato items, fennel, oregano, saffron and pepper flakes; boil, then simmer 7 to 8 minutes and season.
Cook the fresh pasta 3 to 4 minutes until al dente and drain.
Divide the pasta among plates, spoon the sauce over, and finish with Parmesan and parsley.

title: Zack's Pan-Seared "Spykick" Catfish with Tomatillo-Root Vegetable Gratin
ingredients: 1 pound tomatillos, husked, rinsed, and quartered
2 teaspoons chopped fresh basil (1 teaspoon dried)
2 teaspoons chopped fresh thyme (1 teaspoon dried)
1 pound rutabagas or parsnips, peeled and sliced horizontally into ½-inch pieces
1 pound Yukon Gold or other yellow-fleshed potatoes, thinly sliced
8 ounces smoked mozzarella cheese, grated (about ½ cups)
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
GARNISH: chopped roasted yellow pepper (see page 116)
method: Cook the onions, garlic, tomatillos, jalapeños and gratin herbs in the oil over medium-high heat 8 to 10 minutes.
Add the wine, cover and simmer 3 to 4 minutes.
Heat the oven to 375°F. In an oiled 9-by-13-inch dish, layer some tomatillo mix, then rutabaga, cheese and potatoes; repeat and finish with cheese.
Bake uncovered 45 minutes, then covered 10 minutes more; rest covered 8 to 10 minutes.
Mix the paprika, dried thyme and basil, cayenne, salt and pepper, and rub over both sides of the catfish.
Sear the fish in the butter in a very hot skillet 3 to 4 minutes, flip and cook 2 to 3 minutes more until done.
Plate the catfish with squares of gratin and top with roasted yellow pepper.

title: Grilled Sea Bass with Mango–Roasted Red Pepper Relish
ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly ground pepper
2 sea bass (Chilean, if possible) fillets (about 1 pound)
1 cup diced fresh or frozen mango
¼ cup diced roasted red bell pepper (see page 116)
¼ cup chopped sweet onion (Maui, Walla Walla, or Vidalia preferred)
½ teaspoon chopped fresh thyme (¼ teaspoon dried)
method: Mix the vinegar, oil, Worcestershire, salt and pepper in a glass dish, add the fish and refrigerate covered 2 hours.
Stir all the relish ingredients together, season, cover and chill 2 hours.
Grill the fish over hot coals or broil 3 to 4 minutes per side, just until cooked; do not let it dry out.
Serve topped with the relish, with curried couscous alongside.

title: Turkey Piccata with Hot-Sweet Mustard–Lime Sauce
ingredients: ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
6 drops Tabasco or other hot sauce
method: Mix the dried herbs, salt, pepper and flour, and dust both sides of the turkey slices with it.
Heat the oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat; cook the shallots and turkey 2 minutes.
Flip the turkey and add the lime juice, wine, mustard, Worcestershire, Tabasco and capers; cook 2 minutes more.
Move the turkey to a warm plate and let the sauce bubble 1 to 2 minutes to thicken a little.
Spoon the sauce over the turkey, garnish with parsley and lime, and serve with roasted-garlic mashed potatoes.

title: Ricotta-Stuffed Chicken Breast with Roasted Red Bell Pepper Sauce
ingredients: 1 cup chopped roasted red bell peppers (see page 116)
1 teaspoon chopped fresh oregano (½ teaspoon dried)
1 teaspoon chopped fresh basil (½ teaspoon dried)
Kosher salt and red pepper flakes
4 large (7–8 ounces each) bone-in chicken breasts
Kosher salt and red pepper flakes
6 tablespoons chopped sun-dried tomatoes packed in oil
2 tablespoons chopped fresh basil (1 tablespoon dried)
2 tablespoons chopped fresh thyme (1 tablespoon dried)
method: For the sauce, cook the garlic and roasted peppers in the oil over medium heat 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the sherry (or red wine if pouring Pinot Noir), stock, tomato paste, oregano and basil and simmer 4 to 5 minutes; purée, season and keep warm.
Rinse and dry the chicken, cut a deep pocket sideways into each breast, and season with salt and pepper flakes.
Mix the ricotta, sun-dried tomatoes, basil, thyme, shallots and chives; pack into the pockets and dust the breasts with flour.
Heat the oven to 375°F. Brown the breasts in the butter in an ovenproof skillet over medium heat, 3 to 4 minutes a side.
Roast 15 to 18 minutes until cooked through.
Pool the hot sauce on plates, set a breast on top and sprinkle with chives; linguine with basil and olive oil goes well.

title: Marinated Mussels and Roasted Red Bell Peppers
ingredients: 2½ pounds fresh mussels, debearded and rinsed in cold water (see NOTE)
2 red bell peppers, roasted, seeded, peeled, and julienned into 2-inch-long strips (see page 116)
2 teaspoons chopped fresh oregano (1 teaspoon dried)
method: If the mussels still have beards, pull them off under cold running water.
Bring the water and wine to a boil in a large pot and steam the mussels in a basket above it, covered, about 8 minutes until open.
Pick the meat out of the shells into a glass bowl and add 1 cup of the pepper strips (save the rest for another dish).
Whisk the vinegar, oil, oregano, salt, pepper flakes and shallots, pour over the mussels and peppers, and toss.
Cover and chill at least 1 hour; the flavor keeps improving for a few days.
Serve with toothpicks as antipasto, or spooned over chilled greens.

title: "TDF" Gumbo Ma-Gumbo
ingredients: 1 whole cooked Dungeness crab, meat removed (or 8 ounces cooked crab meat)
½ cup fresh or frozen okra, sliced in half lengthwise
1 large green pepper, cored, seeded, and chopped
2 stalks celery, ends removed and chopped
2 ounces ham, tasso, or smoked bacon, diced
4 cups fish stock (or 2 cups clam juice plus 2 cups water)
1 andouille or other spicy sausage, thinly sliced
GARNISH: chopped parsley, minced green onions
method: Peel and devein the shrimp, pick the crab meat, and season the chicken lightly with salt and pepper.
Brown the okra in 1 tablespoon butter over medium heat, 5 to 6 minutes; set aside.
In a large pot, cook the shrimp in 2 tablespoons oil 2 to 3 minutes until pink and remove; then brown the chicken about 10 minutes, turning, and drain on paper towels.
Add the remaining oil and butter, stir in the flour and cook slowly, stirring, until the roux is nutty brown but not scorched.
Raise the heat a little and add the green pepper, celery, onions, garlic, okra and ham; cook about 8 minutes until soft.
Add the stock, tomatoes, seasonings, herbs, filé (ground sassafras), tomato paste and wine; boil, then cover and simmer 1½ hours. It can be made ahead to here.
Thirty minutes before serving add the sausage and chicken; ten minutes before, add the shrimp and crab, and season.
Serve over rice in big bowls with parsley and green onions.

title: Scallop Salad with Anchovies, Radishes, and Almonds
method: Whisk the oils, vinegar, lime juice, saffron, shallots, anchovies and basil in a non-reactive bowl.
Add the scallops and refrigerate 1 hour.
Lift out the scallops and keep the marinade, adjusting its seasoning if needed.
Broil the scallops 2 to 3 minutes per side until just cooked through.
Arrange greens, radishes, almonds and cherry tomatoes on plates, top with the scallops and drizzle with the saved marinade.

title: Dragon-Fire Noodles with Shrimp
serves: 2 to 3 as an entrée or 4 to 6 as an appetizer
ingredients: 1 roasted red bell pepper, peeled and chopped (see page 116)
1 roasted yellow bell pepper, peeled and chopped
GARNISH: white or black sesame seeds and minced green onions
method: Whisk the oils, chile paste, soy, pickled ginger and its juice, lemon juice, vinegar, mint and zest; it should be hot but not numbing.
Add the shrimp and refrigerate 1 to 2 hours.
Boil the noodles in salted water about 2 minutes until al dente, drain, return to the pot and toss with a spoonful of the marinade. Cover.
Simmer the shrimp with the rest of the marinade in a skillet over medium-high heat 1 to 2 minutes until just cooked.
Add shrimp and sauce to the noodles and heat through.
Toss in the roasted peppers and cilantro, top with sesame seeds and green onions, and serve right away.

title: Grilled Salmon with Roasted Poblano–Lime Butter
ingredients: 2½ teaspoons Thai fish sauce or soy sauce
method: Lay the salmon skin side down in a glass dish. Mix the fish sauce, Worcestershire, 1 tablespoon lime juice and sesame oil, pour over, cover and chill 2 hours, turning once.
Roast the chile at 375°F for 45 minutes, turning once, then steam it in a paper bag 15 minutes. Peel, seed and mince.
Blend the butter, 2 teaspoons lime juice, chives and 1 tablespoon of the minced chile for 20 to 30 seconds.
Roll the butter into a small log in waxed paper and refrigerate; take it out 30 minutes before using.
Grill the salmon skin side down over a hot fire 5 minutes, flip and grill 4 to 5 minutes more until cooked through.
Top each fillet with a slice of the butter just before it comes off the grill; polenta cakes and bok choy suit it.

title: Grilled Swordfish with Tomatillo-Cilantro Salsa Verde
ingredients: ½ cup firmly packed cilantro leaves
⅛ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
GARNISH: cilantro sprigs, toasted sesame seeds
method: Blend the marinade ingredients until smooth, pour over the swordfish in a glass dish, and refrigerate 1 to 2 hours.
Roast the tomatillos, jalapeño, garlic and shallot on a sheet at 350°F for 30 to 35 minutes; seed the jalapeño.
Purée the roasted vegetables, then blend in the cilantro, wine, cumin, honey, salt, pepper and pepper flakes.
Bring the salsa to a boil, then cover and simmer 25 to 30 minutes; season, adding a little honey if too sharp.
Grill the swordfish over hot coals 4 to 5 minutes, flip and grill 3 to 4 minutes until just cooked.
Spoon salsa onto plates, set the fish on top and finish with cilantro and sesame seeds. Leftover salsa is good with grilled chicken.

title: Rolled Veal with Prosciutto, Fontina, and Caper Sauce
ingredients: ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
4 ounces thinly sliced Fontina or mozzarella cheese
method: Pound the veal lightly between sheets of waxed paper and season with pepper.
Layer prosciutto, cheese and sage on each piece, roll up from one end and secure with toothpicks or short skewers.
Mix the wine, lime juice, mustard, capers and pepper flakes and set aside.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Brown the rolls on all sides in the butter over medium heat.
Move them to a baking sheet and bake 7 to 8 minutes, until the cheese melts but hasn't run out.
Meanwhile pour the wine mixture into the skillet and simmer to reduce a little; spoon over the veal. Polenta wedges and roasted tomatoes go well.

title: Chilled Summer Peach Soup
ingredients: 1 teaspoon five-spice powder or curry powder (see NOTE)
GARNISH: mint sprigs, plain yogurt, 24 raspberries
method: Blanch the peaches in boiling water for 2 minutes, chill in ice water, then slip off the skins, halve and pit.
Purée the peaches with the honey, yogurt, nectar, Riesling, ginger, mint, chives, zest and five-spice.
Cover and chill at least 2 hours.
Taste and add a little more yogurt if it is too sweet for the wine.
Ladle into bowls and top each with mint, a small spoonful of yogurt and 4 raspberries.

title: Wilted Red Cabbage Salad with Tangerines, Bay Shrimp, and Almonds
serves: 6 to 8 as an appetizer or side dish
ingredients: Kosher salt freshly ground black pepper to taste
¼ cup freshly grated Parmesan or Asiago cheese
method: Halve and core the cabbage, shred it finely, rinse and dry.
Whisk all the dressing ingredients and adjust the seasoning.
Get a wok or large skillet very hot, add 2 to 3 tablespoons of dressing and stir-fry a batch of cabbage about 30 seconds until just wilted and bright.
Move to a bowl and repeat in batches, adding a little dressing each time.
Toss the cabbage with as much of the remaining dressing as you like, plus the almonds, cheese, shrimp and most of the tangerine sections.
Serve warm straight away, topped with the reserved tangerine.

title: Harvest Salad with Pears, Blue Cheese, and Pomegranates
ingredients: 1 cup Riesling, simmered, reduced by half, and cooled
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1 cup peeled and diced Anjou or Bosc pears
method: Simmer the Riesling until reduced by half and let it cool.
Whisk the reduced wine with the mustard, vinegar, salt, pepper and oil.
Divide the greens among small plates.
Top with the blue cheese, walnuts, pomegranate seeds and diced pear.
Drizzle with the dressing and serve.

title: Grilled Vegetable Salad with Major Grey Chutney Dressing
serves: 6 as an appetizer or side dish
ingredients: 3 Japanese eggplants (about 1¼ pounds), ends trimmed, sliced lengthwise in ¼-inch-thick pieces
2 medium radicchio heads, cored, and halved lengthwise
1 bulb fresh fennel, cored, stalks removed, and halved crosswise
1 red bell pepper, cored, seeded, de-ribbed, and halved lengthwise
1 green bell pepper, cored, seeded, de-ribbed and halved lengthwise
1 yellow bell pepper, cored, seeded, de-ribbed, and halved lengthwise
method: Lay the prepared vegetables in a large shallow glass dish.
Blend all the dressing ingredients until smooth, pour over the vegetables and coat them well.
Marinate 2 to 3 hours.
Grill over very hot coals 15 to 18 minutes, turning once; the fennel takes a few minutes longer and can fall apart, so watch it on the grate.
Serve warm, or chill a couple of hours to serve cold.
Cut the peppers and fennel into ½-inch strips and arrange everything on plates.

title: Creole-Style Prawns
ingredients: 1 large tomato, seeded and diced, or one 14½-ounce can chopped tomatoes, drained
¼ cup pitted, chopped Kalamata olives
method: Melt 2 tablespoons butter over medium heat, stir in the flour and cook until smooth and lightly browned.
Whisk in the stock gradually until slightly thickened; set aside.
In a large skillet, cook the green pepper, garlic and onion in the remaining butter 3 to 4 minutes until soft.
Add the tomato, catsup, olives, cayenne, paprika and herbs and simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in the thickened stock, add the prawns, cover and simmer 20 minutes; season.
Serve over white rice in wide bowls, scattered with green onions.

title: Asian-Style Grilled Salmon with Fennel–Pickled Ginger Relish
ingredients: 1 fennel bulb, cored and halved lengthwise
1 tablespoon chopped fresh fennel fronds (see NOTE)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Whisk the marinade, pour over the salmon (skin side down) in a glass dish, cover and chill 1 to 2 hours, turning once.
Roast the fennel at 350°F for 30 minutes, cool a little and chop coarsely.
Mix ¾ cup of the chopped fennel with the fronds, pickled ginger (the pale natural kind, not red-dyed), green onions, lime juice, vinegar, cucumber and sesame seeds; season.
Cover the relish and chill 1 to 2 hours.
Grill the salmon skin side down over hot coals 5 to 6 minutes, flip and cook 4 to 5 minutes, keeping it pink and juicy inside.
Serve with the relish alongside.

title: Hoisin Barbecued Game Hens with Chinese-Style Vegetables
ingredients: ¼ cup mirin (see NOTE), sweet sake, or Riesling
1 tablespoon fermented black beans, rinsed and chopped (see NOTE)
¾ cup julienned red bell pepper
¾ cup julienned yellow bell pepper
½ cup thinly chopped green cabbage
8 ounces bok choy, ends trimmed and halved horizontally
method: Remove the giblets, rinse and dry the hens, split them through breast and backbone, and flatten each half with a firm press of your palm.
Simmer the marinade ingredients 7 to 8 minutes and cool (if skipping black beans, add an extra tablespoon of soy).
Marinate the hens in a sealed bag 2 to 3 hours; keep the marinade for basting.
Set up a charcoal grill for indirect heat with very hot, non-flaming coals pushed to the sides (a gas grill works too).
Grill the hens skin side down, covered, 25 to 30 minutes, basting often; turn and cook another 25 to 30 minutes until the juices run clear.
Stir-fry the onions, garlic, ginger, carrots, celery, peppers, cabbage, bok choy and five-spice in hot oil 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the soy, stock and sugar and stir-fry 2 to 3 minutes more, keeping the vegetables crisp.
Serve the hen halves on a bed of the vegetables.

title: Smoked Pork Chops with Sauerkraut and Green Apples
ingredients: 6 whole juniper berries, crushed with the back of a knife
1 22-ounce jar sauerkraut, rinsed with cold water and squeezed
¾ pound boneless pork loin chops (about ¾-inch thick)
1 pound smoked chicken or pork sausage, halved crosswise
¾ pound Yellow Finn or other yellow-fleshed potatoes, quartered
method: Cook the pancetta in a large pot in its own fat for 4 to 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and onion and cook 5 to 6 minutes more.
Add the juniper, peppercorns, thyme, bay leaf, cloves, caraway, the bottle of Riesling and the cider vinegar.
Stir in the sauerkraut and bury the pork chops, sausage and potatoes in it so they are well covered.
Cover and simmer 50 minutes.
Add the apples and cook 4 to 5 minutes more, then serve in wide bowls.

title: Arugula, Smoked Trout, Roasted Beets, and Caramelized Cashews with Ginger-Chile Dressing
ingredients: 5½ ounces small beets, rinsed and ends trimmed
⅓ cup peeled, finely chopped fresh ginger
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
⅔ cup raw, unsalted cashew halves or macadamia nuts (about ¼ pound) (see NOTE)
½ teaspoon Tabasco or other hot sauce
8 ounces smoked trout, skin removed and cut into 1-inch pieces
method: Roast the beets at 350°F for 1 hour, then peel and dice.
Cook the eggs in boiling water for 90 seconds, peel, and keep only the yolks.
Blend the yolks, ginger, shallots, soy, vinegar, sesame oil, honey, mustard and chiles about 20 seconds, then pour in the olive oil slowly until thick. Add the water and lemon juice and season.
Toast the nuts at 350°F until golden (skip this if using rinsed salted nuts).
Warm the honey in a skillet over low-medium heat 2 to 3 minutes, add the nuts, Tabasco and water and cook until glazed and dry.
Spread the nuts apart on waxed paper to cool.
Arrange arugula on cold plates, top with trout, beets and nuts, and spoon on some dressing (save the rest).

title: Indian Chicken with Nectarine Chutney
ingredients: ½ teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes
2 pounds ripe nectarines, pitted and sliced into 6 pieces each
method: Pull the skin off the breast, thighs and legs and discard it. Rinse and dry the chicken and cut two slits in each breast and thigh.
Rub salt all over and into the slits, and tuck the shallots and garlic inside the cavity.
Whisk the marinade, set the chicken in a foil-lined baking dish, rub the marinade over and inside it, and refrigerate covered 4 to 6 hours or overnight.
For the chutney, boil everything except the nectarines and cilantro in a heavy 4-quart non-reactive pot, then simmer 10 minutes.
Add the nectarines and cook 12 to 14 minutes until thickened and the fruit is tender but not mushy. Remove the cinnamon, stir in the cilantro and chill 3 to 4 hours.
Roast the chicken at 375°F for 70 to 80 minutes, basting often, until it reads 165° to 170°F inside (or cook it on a gas grill over indirect 375°F heat).
Rest it under foil 10 minutes, carve, and serve with the chutney and cilantro sprigs. The chutney keeps 1 to 2 weeks chilled.

title: Spicy Gingered-Carrot Soup
ingredients: 2 stalks celery, ends trimmed and diced
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
GARNISH: chopped fresh cilantro, toasted sesame seeds
method: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and cook the onion, celery, garlic, ginger and carrots 5 to 6 minutes until the onion is translucent.
Add the stock, spices, fish sauce, lime juice, vinegar, peanut butter, sugar, sesame oil, coconut milk (or whole milk) and milk.
Bring to a simmer, cover and cook gently 25 to 30 minutes. Cool slightly.
Purée in batches until smooth and season.
Refrigerate until needed, then bring back to a low boil, or serve it chilled.
Top each bowl with cilantro and sesame seeds.

title: Baked Ham with Spicy Apricot-Orange Glaze and Curried Apple Couscous
ingredients: 4 cups Gewürztraminer or Riesling (two 750-milliliter bottles required)
¼ teaspoon minced chipotle chiles in adobo (see page 175)
1 medium green apple, cored, peeled, seeded, diced, and sprinkled with lemon juice
1 teaspoon cornstarch mixed with 1 teaspoon cold water
method: Trim the ham fat to a ¼-inch layer, score it in a diamond pattern and stud with the cloves. Set in a large foil-lined baking dish.
Bring the glaze ingredients to a boil, then simmer 7 to 8 minutes, stirring; let cool.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Pour the glaze over the ham and pat the brown sugar all over the top.
Bake 1¼ hours, basting often.
Cook the apple with the butter and ½ teaspoon curry powder 7 to 8 minutes; keep warm.
Boil the stock with the remaining curry powder and the cayenne, stir in the couscous, cover off the heat 10 minutes, then fluff and mix in the apple, green onions and almonds; salt to taste.
Keep the ham warm under foil. Simmer the pan juices with the raisins and cornstarch mixture a couple of minutes to thicken.
Slice the ham, spoon the sauce over and serve the couscous alongside.

title: Louis-Style Shrimp in Endive "Boats"
ingredients: ⅓ cup prepared seafood cocktail sauce
2 tablespoons minced cornichons or dill pickles
2 teaspoons chopped fresh tarragon (1 teaspoon dried)
method: Mix the sour cream, cocktail sauce, cornichons, green onions, herbs, salt, pepper and hot sauce.
Fold in the shrimp, season, and chill covered at least 1 hour.
Trim the endive and ease off the large outer leaves whole (save the small hearts for something else). Rinse, dry and keep cold.
Arrange the leaves in circles on plates or a platter.
Spoon a little shrimp into each leaf and sprinkle with parsley.

title: Smoked Oyster–Cream Cheese Wontons
ingredients: 7 1½ ounces (2 cans) smoked oysters, drained of oil
½ teaspoon jalapeño Tabasco or other hot sauce
GARNISH: minced lemon zest, minced fresh chives
method: Heat the oven to 350°F. Press the wonton wrappers into an oiled mini-muffin tin so they line each cup.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes and let rest.
Pulse the oysters, cream cheese, Worcestershire, Tabasco, zest, chives and lemon juice 15 to 20 seconds until just blended; season.
Spoon the filling into the wonton cups.
Bake at 375°F another 10 to 15 minutes until golden.
Unmold onto a platter and sprinkle with lemon zest and chives. Extra filling keeps a week or more as a cracker spread.

title: Lobster Salad with Apricot-Walnut Vinaigrette
serves: 2 to 4 as an appetizer or light entrée
ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Plunge the live lobster into a large pot of rapidly boiling water, cover and cook 7 to 8 minutes.
Drain it, then chill on a plate 1 to 2 hours.
Mix the vinegar, apricot nectar, both oils, Worcestershire and tarragon.
Twist off the claws, open the body and scoop out the green tomalley; whisk 1½ teaspoons of it into the dressing and season.
Pick all the meat from the tail and claws.
Arrange greens and lobster on cold plates with the cherry tomatoes and drizzle with the dressing.

title: Chicken Paprika with Dried Peach and Almond Relish
ingredients: ¾ cup chopped dried peaches or apricots
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Stir the relish ingredients together and chill 1 to 2 hours.
Rinse and dry the chicken and season with salt, hot paprika, sage and lemon zest.
Brown the chicken on both sides in the butter and 1 tablespoon oil over medium heat; set aside on paper towels.
Add more oil if needed and cook the onions and garlic 3 to 4 minutes until translucent.
Add the mushrooms, marjoram, sweet paprika and caraway and cook 3 to 4 minutes, then stir in the stock and sour cream.
Return the chicken, cover and simmer 12 to 14 minutes; season.
Plate the chicken, spoon the sauce over and top with the relish; serve with buttered noodles or spaetzle.

title: Duck Breasts with Honey, Ginger, and Lavender
ingredients: ⅛ teaspoon mixed whole peppercorns, crushed
½ teaspoon chopped fresh tarragon (¼ teaspoon dried)
1 tablespoon unsalted butter at room temperature
method: Split each breast in two, trim the excess fat and score an X in the skin.
Coat with half the crushed pepper, the Worcestershire, ¼ teaspoon ginger, the lavender and shallot slices; cover and chill 2 to 3 hours.
Boil the wine, stock, vanilla, remaining ginger and pepper, and the shallots taken off the duck; simmer until reduced by half.
Add the honey and tarragon and keep reducing to a sauce. Off the heat, swirl in the butter, season and keep warm.
Cook the duck skin side down in the oil over medium heat 5 to 6 minutes until browned, then turn and cook 2 to 4 minutes for medium-rare with pink juices.
Slice on an angle, fan on plates, spoon the sauce over and add tarragon; wild rice with dried cherries suits it.

title: Chilled Corn and Sun-Dried Tomato Chowder with Goat Cheese–Chive Croutons
ingredients: 2 cups chopped sweet onions (Maui, Vidalia, or Walla Walla)
1 tablespoon chopped fresh tarragon (½ tablespoon dried)
¾ cup sun-dried tomato halves (rehydrated in water and drained)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 sourdough baguette, cut on the diagonal into twelve ¼-inch slices
method: Cut the kernels off the cobs with a serrated knife (about 2 cups) and keep the cobs.
Cook the onions, tarragon, cumin, turmeric and 1 teaspoon of the zest in the oil 7 to 8 minutes.
Add the corn, cobs, stock and wine, bring to a hard boil, then cover and simmer 12 minutes. Remove the cobs.
Purée in batches with the roasted garlic, lemon juice and sour cream, then pulse in the sun-dried tomatoes until roughly chopped.
Season and chill 3 to 4 hours, thinning with a little stock if needed (it can also be served hot).
Mash the goat cheese with the chives and remaining ½ teaspoon zest; spread on the bread and broil 5 to 6 minutes until just colouring.
Ladle the soup into bowls, lean two crossed croutons in each and sprinkle with tarragon.

title: Scallop and Smoked Salmon Cakes with Rémoulade
ingredients: ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1 tablespoon chopped fresh parsley (½ tablespoon dried)
½ tablespoon minced fresh chives (¼ tablespoon dried)
1½ tablespoon chopped fresh thyme (¼ tablespoon dried)
1½ tablespoons chopped cornichons or dill pickles, drained
¼ pound smoked salmon pieces, skin removed
⅓ cup finely chopped yellow or green bell pepper
⅓ cup finely chopped red bell pepper
⅓ cup finely chopped yellow onions
GARNISH: chopped red and yellow bell pepper
method: Blend the egg, lemon juice, mustard, salt and pepper, then pour in the oil slowly with the motor running until thick.
Blend in the tomato paste, herbs, capers, cornichons and zest; chill covered.
Pulse the scallops and smoked salmon about 10 times into small pieces, not a paste.
Mix the seafood with the peppers, onion, chives and ¼ cup of the rémoulade.
Combine the bread crumbs and parsley and add just enough to hold the mixture together; shape into 12 small patties.
Heat the oven to 400°F. Brown the patties in butter in a non-stick pan over low-medium heat 2 to 3 minutes a side, pressing lightly.
Transfer to a baking sheet and bake about 12 minutes until cooked through.
Serve two cakes per plate on greens, drizzled with rémoulade and sprinkled with chopped peppers.

title: Crab, Jícama, and Mango Salad with Lemon-Curry Dressing
ingredients: 1 pound crab meat, picked over for shells
¾ cup diced fresh or frozen mango
Juice of 1 lemon (Meyer lemon, if possible)
⅓ cup mayonnaise or sour cream
⅛ teaspoon fresh ground black pepper
12 leaves butter lettuce, rinsed and dried
method: Combine the crab, mango, chives and jícama in a non-reactive bowl.
Whisk the dressing ingredients together.
Fold the dressing into the crab and refrigerate at least 2 hours; season.
Set two lettuce leaves on each plate.
Stir the salad, spoon it onto the leaves, and finish with chives and a lemon slice.

title: Risotto with Squash, Oyster Mushrooms, and Peppered Jack Cheese
serves: 4 to 6 as an appetizer or 2 to 3 as an entrée
ingredients: 1½ pounds seeded, sliced butternut squash (see NOTE)
4 tablespoons (¼ cup) unsalted butter or olive oil
2 teaspoons chopped fresh basil (1 teaspoon dried)
½ cup grated peppered Jack cheese
method: Bake the squash at 375°F for 40 to 45 minutes until tender, then peel and cut into ½-inch dice. Keep 1¼ cups warm in foil.
Brown the mushrooms in 1 tablespoon butter or oil over medium heat 5 to 7 minutes; set aside.
Heat the remaining fat and cook the shallots, garlic, herbs and rice 3 to 5 minutes until the rice looks translucent.
Add the wine and let it absorb, then add the hot stock ½ cup at a time, stirring until each addition is absorbed.
In the last 5 minutes stir in the cheese, squash and mushrooms.
When the rice is al dente, take off the heat, add the chives and season. Serve in warm bowls with cherry tomatoes.
protein: butternut squash and mushrooms (vegetarian with chicken stock)

title: Rigatoni with Shiitake Mushrooms, Fennel, and Oysters
ingredients: 1 pound dried rigatoni or other small pasta
¼ cup chopped fresh basil (2 tablespoons dried)
½ cup fish stock or clam juice
¾ cup seeded, chopped plum tomatoes
Kosher salt and freshly ground white pepper
method: Boil the rigatoni in salted water 7 to 8 minutes until al dente; drain, return to the pot with a little oil and keep warm.
Heat the olive oil in a sauté pan over medium heat and cook the garlic, shallots, mushrooms, fennel and basil 5 to 6 minutes.
Pour in the wine, fish stock and cream and simmer 8 to 10 minutes to reduce slightly.
Add the oysters and tomatoes and warm through; season.
Toss the sauce with the pasta, heat thoroughly and serve on warm plates with basil leaves.

title: Spinach Fettuccine with Sea Bass and Lemongrass-Coconut Cream Sauce
serves: 5 to 6 as an appetizer or 3 to 4 as an entrée
ingredients: 1 stalk fresh lemongrass or 1 teaspoon minced lime zest
¾ cup broccoli florets, steamed or microwaved
⅛ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1½ pounds fresh sea bass, cut crosswise into ½-inch slices
1 teaspoon cornstarch mixed with 1 teaspoon cold water (optional)
½ cup seeded and chopped tomatoes
method: Strip the lemongrass of its outer leaves and dark green top, trim and mince the pale part very finely; keep 1½ tablespoons.
Cook the shallots, ginger and lemongrass in the oil over medium heat 2 minutes, then add the mushrooms for 4 to 5 minutes more.
Add the wine, raise the heat and reduce by half.
Stir in the broccoli, coconut milk, saffron, turmeric, salt, pepper and 1 tablespoon chives; simmer steadily 5 to 6 minutes.
Lower to a gentle simmer, add the sea bass, cover and cook 10 minutes, turning once. Season; thicken with the cornstarch slurry for 2 minutes if wanted.
Cook the fettuccine in boiling salted water 6 to 7 minutes until al dente; drain and toss with a little oil.
Combine the pasta with the sauce and fish, heat through and ladle into warm bowls topped with pine nuts, tomatoes and the remaining chives.

title: Broiled Monkfish with Fennel, Hazelnuts, and Orange Sauce
ingredients: 2 pounds monkfish or sea bass or grouper fillets
3 cups thinly sliced fennel (about 2 bulbs with core removed)
½ teaspoon cornstarch mixed with ½ teaspoon cold water
GARNISH: toasted, peeled, and lightly chopped hazelnuts; thinly sliced orange; and remaining fennel fronds
method: Rub the fish with 1 tablespoon oil, scatter over 1 teaspoon curry powder and the chopped fronds, season and set on a broiler pan.
Sauté the shallots, sliced fennel, fennel seed and ½ teaspoon curry powder in 1½ tablespoons oil over medium heat 7 to 8 minutes, stirring often.
Add the orange juice, wine, stock and zest, boil, then simmer until reduced by half, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch mixture, simmer until lightly thickened and season.
Broil the fish 8 to 10 minutes until just cooked through.
Spoon the sauce over the fish and finish with hazelnuts, orange slices and fennel fronds; serve with herbed rice.

title: Cold Poached Salmon with Tarragon-Mint Aïoli
ingredients: 2 cups fish stock, clam juice, or chicken stock
½ teaspoon kosher salt (if using unsalted stock)
1½ tablespoons chopped fresh tarragon (¾ tablespoon dried)
2 tablespoons chopped fresh mint (1 tablespoon dried)
½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
½ cup (or more) extra-virgin olive oil
method: Bring the wine, stock, bay leaf, carrots, celery, onions, peppercorns and salt to a steady simmer in a large sauté pan.
Lay in the salmon skin side down, cover and simmer gently about 12 minutes until cooked through.
Lift out the salmon and chill 2 to 3 hours (the freezer works for a quick chill).
Process the tarragon, mint, lime juice, vinegar, capers, egg yolks, roasted garlic, salt and pepper for 1 minute.
With the machine running, drizzle in the oil until emulsified, adding a little more if needed; refrigerate covered for an hour.
Plate the salmon with alternating lemon and lime slices and a dollop of aïoli; the preserved lemon–pine nut couscous (page 122) goes well alongside.

title: Three-Seed Crusted Ahi with Lima Beans, Corn, and Pancetta
ingredients: 1 pound shelled fresh or frozen lima beans
½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
method: Roast the pepper at 350°F for 30 minutes, steam it in a paper bag 8 to 10 minutes, then peel, seed and dice.
Chop the pancetta and fry in 1 teaspoon oil over medium heat 8 to 10 minutes until lightly browned; drain on paper.
Boil the stock with the shallots, add the lima beans and simmer uncovered 15 to 17 minutes until just past al dente.
Pour off most of the stock and stir in the corn, pancetta and roasted pepper; keep warm.
Coat the ahi with 1½ tablespoons oil, then press on the mixed seeds, salt and pepper.
Sear in a very hot dry pan 2 to 3 minutes per side so the centre stays very rare; slice thinly.
Spoon the beans and a little liquid onto plates, top with the sliced ahi and scatter with green onions.

title: Herb and Spice Roasted Cornish Game Hens
serves: 3 to 6 as an entrée, depending on appetite
ingredients: 3 Cornish game hens, livers and gizzards removed, and rinsed
½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
method: Heat the oven to 350°F and set the hens in a large ovenproof dish.
Tuck a garlic clove, a few shallot pieces and a rosemary sprig into each cavity and rub the cavities with ½ teaspoon of the salt.
Whisk the two mustards with the fines herbes, paprika, fennel seed, pepper, red pepper flakes and remaining ½ teaspoon salt.
Coat the hens all over with the mustard paste.
Roast 1¼ hours until the juices run clear; serve with buttered corn and braised Swiss chard.

title: Braised Pork with Apples, Mushrooms, and Calvados
ingredients: 1½ pounds pork stew meat (from the shoulder), cut into 1-inch pieces
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1 tablespoon chopped fresh tarragon (½ tablespoon dried)
1 tablespoon chopped fresh thyme (½ tablespoon dried)
⅓ cup Calvados (apple brandy) or other brandy
1 cup peeled, cored, and sliced Mcintosh apples
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
GARNISH: toasted, diced almonds; chopped parsley
method: Cook the mushrooms, onions, pancetta and garlic in the butter over medium heat 5 to 7 minutes until the onions are translucent.
Season the pork with the salt and pepper, add it with the tarragon, thyme and poppyseed and brown lightly, 8 to 10 minutes.
Add the wine, Calvados and stock, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 40 minutes.
Stir in the sour cream and simmer covered 15 minutes more to reduce.
Add the apples and cook just 3 to 4 minutes so they keep some crunch; season.
Plate with almonds and parsley on top; spinach fettuccine or spaetzle alongside.

title: Veal Roast with Dijon-Tinged Vegetable Sauce
ingredients: 1 5-pound boneless leg of veal, rolled and tied
¾ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1 tablespoon chopped fresh oregano (½ tablespoon dried)
1 tablespoon chopped fresh thyme (½ tablespoon dried)
2 cups chopped and seeded fresh tomatoes
GARNISH: chopped parsley, minced lemon zest
method: Season the veal with the salt, pepper, paprika and fennel seed and let it rest.
Brown the roast on all sides, ends included, in 2 tablespoons butter over medium-high heat; set aside.
Cook the onions, garlic, celery, carrots, oregano, thyme and bay leaves in the remaining butter 5 minutes, then add the tomatoes for 1 to 2 minutes more.

Heat the oven to 325°F. Spread the vegetables in a foil-lined 13-by-9-by-2-inch roasting pan, set the veal on top, pour over the stock and wine and spread 2 tablespoons mustard on the roast (it can wait, refrigerated, up to 6 hours here).
Roast about 2½ hours to an internal temperature of 165° to 170°F, basting now and then.
Cut the string and tent the veal in foil. Purée the pan vegetables with the last tablespoon of mustard, season, thin with stock if needed and reheat.
Spoon the sauce onto plates, top with thin slices of veal and sprinkle with parsley and lemon zest; roasted parsley-garlic potatoes go well.

title: Grilled Rabbit with Preserved Lemon–Toasted Pine Nut Couscous
ingredients: 3 cups cooked couscous (cooked according to package instructions)
1 cup seeded, chopped preserved lemons with skin on (recipe follows)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
2 whole rabbits, rinsed and patted dry
2 tablespoons chopped fresh mint (1 tablespoon dried)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Toss the couscous with the pine nuts, preserved lemon, roasted garlic, mint, green onions and oil, fluffing with a fork; season. Serve warm or at room temperature.
Remove the giblets, cut off the rabbit legs and carve the loins from the carcass; put the pieces in a sealable bag.
Whisk the oil, mustard, cumin, wine, mint and green onions, season, pour over the rabbit and refrigerate 2 to 3 hours or overnight.
Pat the rabbit dry and keep the marinade for basting.
Grill the legs over hot coals 12 to 15 minutes, turning once and basting, then add the loins for 4 to 6 minutes a side until barely white inside.
Rest the loins; give the legs a couple more minutes if the juices don't yet run clear.
Slice the loins thinly beside a mound of couscous, share out the leg pieces and serve with green beans.

title: Preserved Lemons
method: Scrub the lemons and soak them in cold water in a non-reactive bowl for 3 days, changing the water daily.
Cut 4 lengthwise slits in each lemon, stopping short of the top and bottom.
Ease each lemon open and sprinkle ½ teaspoon salt into the centre.
Sterilize 6 canning jars and pack each with 2 lemons, ½ cinnamon stick, 2 cloves and 3 peppercorns.
Divide the remaining salt between the jars, add ½ tablespoon lemon juice to each and top up with boiling water.
Seal and leave 2 weeks or longer in a cool, dark place; they keep indefinitely.

title: Risotto with Roasted Shallots, Portobello Mushrooms, Radicchio, and Parmesan
serves: 6 as an appetizer or 4 as an entrée
ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
½ pound portobello mushrooms, diced (about 2 cups)
1 tablespoon chopped fresh thyme (½ tablespoon dried)
method: Heat the oven to 350°F. Trim and peel the shallots, halve them, toss with 1 tablespoon oil, salt and pepper, wrap loosely in foil and roast 65 minutes; leave wrapped.
Heat the remaining oil with the butter over medium heat and cook the mushrooms and onions 2 to 3 minutes, stirring.
Add the rice and thyme and cook 4 to 5 minutes more, stirring often.
Add the wine carefully and let it evaporate, then add the hot stock ½ cup at a time, stirring until each is mostly absorbed, until the rice is al dente.
Stir in the radicchio and tomatoes for 1 to 2 minutes to wilt, then the Parmesan.
Serve very hot in bowls topped with the roasted shallots and chives.

title: Grilled Salmon with Mushrooms, Sweet Onions, and Pinot Noir Sauce
ingredients: 1 tablespoon chopped fresh thyme (½ tablespoon dried)
3 cups sliced portobello mushrooms, inner gills removed
3 cups sliced sweet onions (Vidalia, Maui, or Walla Walla)
2 tablespoons chopped fresh thyme (1 tablespoon dried)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
½ teaspoon cornstarch mixed with ½ teaspoon cold water
method: Whisk the marinade ingredients together, marinate the salmon 2 hours, then pat dry.
Sauté the mushrooms, sweet onions, 1 tablespoon thyme and the mustard seed in 3 tablespoons oil over medium-high heat 7 to 8 minutes until the onions are translucent; season and keep warm.
Soften the shallots in 1 tablespoon oil 2 to 3 minutes, add the Pinot Noir and reduce by half.
Add the stock, the other tablespoon of thyme, the Dijon and cornstarch slurry and reduce until the sauce coats a wooden spoon.
Off the heat, stir in the butter and season; keep warm.
Grill the salmon over hot coals 4 to 5 minutes per side depending on thickness (or broil 6 to 7 minutes), without overcooking.
Bed the mushroom-onion mix on warm plates, set the salmon on top and spoon over the sauce; brown sugar–glazed parslied carrots alongside.

title: Grilled Ahi with Ginger–Black Bean Sauce
ingredients: ¼ cup sake or dry white wine
1½ cups Pinot Noir or other light-bodied red wine
2½ tablespoons whole fermented black beans, rinsed in cold water, or 1 tablespoon Chinese black bean sauce
1 teaspoon wasabi powder, mixed with 1 teaspoon cold water
½ teaspoon cornstarch mixed with ½ teaspoon cold water
2 tablespoons unsalted butter at room temperature (optional)
GARNISH: toasted sesame seeds, cilantro sprigs
method: Whisk the soy, sake, sesame oil, vinegar, ginger and green onions; seal with the ahi in a plastic bag and refrigerate 1 to 2 hours, turning now and then.
Sweat the shallots and ginger in the oil over low-medium heat 2 to 3 minutes, add the wine, boil briefly, then simmer until reduced by three-quarters.
Add the stock, black beans, vinegar and wasabi and reduce by half.
Strain, discard the solids, return the liquid to the pan with the cornstarch slurry and cilantro and reduce to thicken slightly; whisk in the butter and keep warm off the heat.
Grill the ahi over very hot coals 2 to 3 minutes, turn and give it 1 to 2 minutes more so it stays very rare inside; slice thinly.
Pool the sauce on plates, lay the ahi over it, scatter sesame seeds and cilantro and serve with jasmine rice and Chinese-style vegetables (page 79).

title: Asian-Style Grilled Squab with Fennel, Bok Choy, and Chanterelle Mushrooms
ingredients: 1 sweet onion (Vidalia, Maui, or Walla Walla), peeled and thinly sliced
1 fresh fennel bulb, cored and cut into ½-inch pieces, with leafy fronds reserved for garnish
4 ounces fresh chanterelle mushrooms (or 1 ounce dried and reconstituted in warm water), lightly rinsed and sliced
¼ cup julienned red bell pepper
¼ cup julienned yellow bell pepper
2 small bunches baby bok choy, ends trimmed, rinsed, and cut into ¼-inch pieces
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Halve each squab through breast and backbone, cut the breasts off the bone in one piece and separate the leg-thigh pieces; discard the wings and carcass or keep for stock.
Whisk the marinade ingredients, add the squab pieces in a sealable bag and refrigerate 2 to 3 hours.
Pat the squab dry, keeping the marinade for basting.

Cook the onion and fennel in the olive oil over low-medium heat 6 to 7 minutes, add the chanterelles, ginger and peppers for 4 minutes, then the bok choy, mustard seed and curry powder for 3 to 4 minutes; season and keep warm.
Over hot coals grill the leg-thigh pieces skin side down 2 to 3 minutes, add the breasts skin side down for 2 to 3 minutes, then turn everything for 1 to 2 minutes until the breasts are juicy rare.
Rest the breasts in foil and give the legs 2 to 3 minutes more to rare or medium-rare; don't overcook.
Divide the vegetables between plates, top each with a breast and a leg-thigh piece, garnish with fennel fronds and serve with vanilla-scented jasmine rice.

title: Grilled Pork Tenderloin with Pomegranate Sauce
ingredients: ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
2 tablespoons unsalted butter at room temperature
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Whisk the marinade ingredients, pour over the tenderloins in a sealable bag and refrigerate 3 to 4 hours; pat dry and keep the marinade for basting.
Soften the shallots in the oil over medium heat 2 to 3 minutes without browning.
Add the Pinot Noir, port, vinegar and peppercorns, boil, then simmer until reduced by half.
Add the pomegranate concentrate, orange juice, stock and star anise and reduce by half again, until the sauce coats a wooden spoon; sweeten with honey.
Strain, swirl in the butter, season and keep warm.
Grill the pork over hot coals 5 to 6 minutes per side to medium-rare, basting occasionally; slice.
Plate the pork under the sauce with mint sprigs and pomegranate seeds scattered around; serve with couscous.

title: Thai-Style Grilled Lamb with Raspberry-Mango Relish
ingredients: 3 tablespoons whole fermented black beans, rinsed in cold water, or 1 tablespoon Chinese black bean sauce
3 tablespoons chopped lemongrass, outer leaves and stems removed (optional)
2 tablespoons chopped fresh mint (1 tablespoon dried)
1 6- to 7-pound whole leg of lamb, boned, butterflied, and trimmed of excess fat (about 4½ pounds boned and trimmed)
¾ cup diced fresh or frozen mango
½ cup chopped sweet onions (Vidalia, Maui, or Walla Walla)
method: Whisk the marinade ingredients together.
Marinate the lamb in a large sealable bag in the refrigerator at least 3 to 4 hours, turning so every side gets coated; pat dry.
Mix the relish ingredients and chill 2 to 3 hours for the flavours to blend; adjust seasoning.
Grill the lamb over hot but not flaming coals 7 to 8 minutes per side to medium-rare, watching that the sweet marinade doesn't char (or roast at 450°F).
Carve thinly, spoon the relish over, add cilantro sprigs and serve with turmeric-infused couscous.

title: Coffee- and Spice-Rubbed Lamb with Coffee-Vanilla Sauce
ingredients: 2 teaspoons chopped fresh rosemary (1 teaspoon dried)
4 boneless, tied lamb sirloin rolls (about 2 pounds) or 8 double-thick lamb chops (about 6 pounds), trimmed of fat
1 teaspoon cornstarch mixed with 1 teaspoon cold water
1 tablespoon unsalted butter at room temperature (optional)
Kosher salt and freshly ground pepper
method: Stir the garlic, mint, ground coffee, ¼ cup oil and ⅓ cup wine together in a non-reactive bowl.
Grind the peppercorns, cumin, mustard and coriander seeds, rosemary and salt in a mortar or spice grinder and whisk into the coffee mixture.
Rub the marinade all over the lamb in a glass dish, cover and refrigerate 3 to 4 hours; wipe off most, but not all, of it with paper towels.
Cook the mushrooms and shallots in 2 tablespoons oil over medium heat 4 to 5 minutes, add the 1½ cups wine, vanilla bean and mint, boil, then simmer until reduced by half.
Stir in the stock, brewed coffee and honey and reduce by half again; remove the vanilla bean and thicken with the cornstarch slurry.
Off the heat swirl in the butter, season and keep warm.
Grill the lamb over a hot fire 7 to 8 minutes per side to medium-rare; plate with the sauce on top and mint sprigs.

title: Roast Leg of Veal with Wild Mushroom Sauce and Walnuts
ingredients: 1 4- to 5-pound boned leg of veal, rolled and tied
½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1 red onion, peeled and thinly sliced
2 cups sliced portobello mushrooms, stems trimmed, inner gills removed
3 cups sliced shiitake mushrooms, stems trimmed
1 cup Pinot Noir or other red wine
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
GARNISH: chopped parsley, whole roasted shiitake mushrooms
method: Rub the veal with the paprika, salt and pepper; heat the oven to 325°F.
Cook the onion, mushrooms and herbs in the olive oil over medium heat 4 to 5 minutes until the onion is translucent, then spoon into a foil-lined roasting pan big enough for the veal.
Brown the roast lightly on all sides in the butter in the same pan and set it on the mushroom bed.
Pour over the wine and 1¼ cups stock and roast about 2 hours to an internal temperature of 170°F, basting occasionally.
Cut the string and tent the veal in foil; purée the mushroom mixture until smooth, thin with stock if you like, season and keep warm.
Slice the veal over a pool of mushroom sauce, scatter with walnuts, parsley and whole mushrooms; glazed dilled carrots and roasted potato quarters go well.

title: White Bean Soup with Escargots and Olive Relish
serves: 6 to 8 as an appetizer or 4 as an entrée
ingredients: 12 ounces white beans (such as Great Northern), rinsed and picked over
¾ cup cored, chopped fresh fennel
1 cup plum tomatoes, seeded and chopped
1 pound Yukon gold or new potatoes, diced
2 teaspoons chopped fresh rosemary (1 teaspoon dried)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
¾ teaspoon chopped fresh rosemary (⅓ teaspoon dried)
method: Soak the beans overnight in cold water, then drain and discard any discoloured ones.
Sauté the carrot, celery, onions, fennel and garlic in 1½ tablespoons oil over medium heat 5 to 6 minutes in a large pot.
Add the beans, stock, tomatoes, potatoes, rosemary, mustard seed and fennel seed, boil, then cover and simmer 45 to 55 minutes until the beans are al dente; season.
Stir the olive paste, shallots, balsamic and rosemary together for the relish.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil, cook the garlic and escargots 3 to 4 minutes until warmed through, add the Pernod and cook 1 minute until it evaporates.
Ladle the soup into hot bowls, dollop relish on top, arrange the escargots around it and add rosemary sprigs.

title: Herb and Sun-Dried Tomato Calzone with Hot Sausage, Prosciutto, and Okra
ingredients: 1 cup warm tap water (110° to 115°F on an instant-read thermometer)
¼ cup plus ½ tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil
2½ tablespoons chopped mixed herbs (parsley, basil, oregano)
2½ tablespoons chopped sun-dried tomatoes packed in oil
1 cup fresh or frozen okra, sliced in half lengthwise
3 tablespoons chopped fresh basil (1½ tablespoons dried)
1 tablespoon chopped fresh oregano (½ tablespoon dried)
12 ounces hot Italian, andouille, or chorizo sausage, cut into ¼-inch slices
1 cup grated Asiago or Parmesan cheese
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Dissolve the sugar and yeast in the warm water and leave 8 to 10 minutes until foamy, then stir in ¼ cup oil for 15 to 20 seconds.
Pulse the flour, salt and pepper in a food processor, add the herbs and sun-dried tomatoes, then pour in the yeast mixture with the motor running until a ball forms, 30 to 45 seconds.
Knead on a floured surface 5 to 8 minutes until smooth and elastic, adjusting with warm water or flour as needed.
Turn the dough in a bowl coated with ½ tablespoon oil, cover with plastic and let rise in a warm spot about 1½ hours until doubled.
Sauté the okra, mushrooms, celery, carrots, onions, garlic, basil and oregano in 1 tablespoon oil over medium heat 7 to 8 minutes.
Brown the sausage slices in a non-stick pan 5 to 6 minutes and blot dry.
Whisk the tomato sauce, paste, filé and cayenne, then fold in the sausage, prosciutto, cheese and vegetables; season.
Heat the oven to 450°F. Punch down the dough, divide in four and roll into 8- to 9-inch rounds; brush with oil.
Fill one half of each round, fold over, roll and crimp the edges, press with a fork, brush with oil and prick the tops.
Bake on a cornmeal-dusted sheet on the top rack 16 to 18 minutes until golden, shielding the edges with foil if they darken; serve with basil leaves.

title: Veal-Stuffed Manicotti with Roasted Yellow Pepper Pesto
ingredients: 1 tablespoon chopped fresh oregano (½ tablespoon dried)
1 tablespoon chopped fresh marjoram (½ tablespoon dried)
1 10-ounce package frozen chopped spinach, thawed and well drained
½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
2 roasted yellow bell peppers (see page 116), peeled and seeded
¼ cup lightly toasted pine nuts
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 tablespoon chopped fresh oregano (½ tablespoon dried)
1 tablespoon chopped fresh basil (½ tablespoon dried)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Soften the onions and garlic in 1 tablespoon oil over medium heat 4 to 5 minutes, add the veal, oregano, marjoram, fennel seed and Worcestershire and cook 5 to 6 minutes until no longer pink; drain the fat.
Stir in the spinach and eggs for 2 to 3 minutes, then off the heat mix in the mozzarella, ricotta and bread crumbs; season with the salt, pepper, pepper flakes and cinnamon and cool.
Boil the manicotti 7 to 8 minutes (or per the package) until firm but cooked, hold in cold water, drain and pat dry.
Fill the tubes with the veal mixture, lay in an oiled baking dish and refrigerate.
Blend the roasted peppers, shallot, pine nuts and Worcestershire until smooth, stream in the oil, season and chill; bring to room temperature to serve.

For the sauce, cook the onions and garlic in ½ tablespoon oil 5 to 6 minutes, add the sherry, tomato sauce, tomatoes, paste, oregano, basil, sugar and pepper flakes and cook 7 to 8 minutes, stirring; season.
Pour the sauce over the manicotti, cover with foil and bake at 350°F for 30 minutes, then top with the grated mozzarella and bake uncovered 15 minutes more.
Serve two manicotti per plate with a dollop of pesto and a sprinkle of oregano.

title: Chicken Cacciatore with Kalamata Olives and Fennel
ingredients: ¾ tablespoon all-purpose flour plus more as needed
1 fennel bulb, cored and thinly sliced (about 2 cups)
1 tablespoon chopped fresh sage (½ tablespoon dried)
1 tablespoon chopped fresh rosemary (½ tablespoon dried)
½ cup pitted, chopped Kalamata olives
method: Rinse and dry the chicken, season with salt and pepper flakes and dust lightly with flour.
Brown the chicken on all sides in the butter and oil in a large stockpot over medium heat; drain on paper towels.
In the same pot sauté the garlic, onions, mushrooms, fennel, carrots, sage and rosemary 7 to 8 minutes.
Return the chicken with the stock, wine, tomatoes, tomato paste and olives, cover and simmer 50 to 55 minutes.
Lift out the chicken, reduce the sauce 15 minutes uncovered, then put the chicken back to heat through; season.
Serve in bowls with parsley and wedges of baked polenta topped with Parmesan.

title: Grilled Pork Tenderloin with Sun-Dried Cherry-Blood Orange Sauce
ingredients: ⅔ cup blood orange (or regular orange) juice
½ teaspoon blood orange (or regular orange) zest
⅛ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1 teaspoon cornstarch mixed with 1 teaspoon cold water
1 tablespoon unsalted butter at room temperature (optional)
GARNISH: thin slices of blood orange
method: Whisk the marinade ingredients in a non-reactive bowl and pour over the tenderloins in a glass dish; refrigerate covered 3 to 4 hours, turning once.
Pat the pork dry, keep the marinade, and spread the mustard over the meat.
Simmer the marinade with the stock and cherries in a large pan about 15 minutes until it coats a wooden spoon.
Thicken slightly with the cornstarch slurry, whisk in the butter if using and keep warm.
Grill over hot coals 6 to 7 minutes, turn and cook 4 to 5 minutes more to medium-rare and juicy.
Slice, spoon over the sauce and garnish with blood orange slices.

title: Paella with Peppered Chicken, Spicy Sausage, and Escargots
ingredients: ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
2 spicy sausages (spicy Italian, andouille, or chorizo), cut in ½-inch slices
8 ounces mussels, debearded and rinsed (see page 58)
1 large roasted red pepper, diced (see page 116)
¾ cup fresh or defrosted frozen peas
method: Rinse and dry the thighs, rub with ¼ teaspoon salt and the pepper and rest a few minutes.
Brown the chicken on both sides in ½ tablespoon oil in a non-stick pan; drain on paper towels.

In a paella pan fry the sausage and escargots in the remaining 2 tablespoons oil 3 to 4 minutes, add the garlic and onions for 3 minutes, then the rice, remaining ¼ teaspoon salt, saffron, paprika and turmeric and stir 5 minutes to coat.
Add the wine and let it evaporate, then the stock; bring to a boil and drop to a simmer.
Nestle the chicken and mussels over the rice, cover and cook 17 to 18 minutes until the chicken is done and the rice al dente.
Scatter the roasted pepper, parsley and peas on top, cover 2 to 3 minutes just to warm, keeping the peas bright; season.
Finish with more parsley and serve from the pan, one thigh each with the mussels and escargots shared out.
protein: chicken thighs, spicy sausage, escargots, mussels

title: Basil Fettuccine with Sun-Dried Tomatoes, Olives, and Prosciutto
serves: 5 to 6 as an appetizer or 2 to 4 as an entrée
ingredients: 1¼ cups sliced crimini or shiitake mushrooms
¾ cup Zinfandel or other red wine
1 cup julienned sun-dried tomatoes packed in oil
⅔ cup pitted, chopped Kalamata olives
3 tablespoons chopped fresh basil (1½ tablespoons dried)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
1¼ pounds fresh or dried basil fettuccine noodles
½ cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese
method: Cook the garlic, onions and mushrooms in the oil over medium heat 3 to 4 minutes until the onions are translucent.
Add the wine, sun-dried tomatoes, tomato paste, tomato sauce, olives, basil, fennel seed and balsamic and simmer, stirring, about 8 minutes until slightly thickened.
Keep warm over low heat, loosening with more wine if it gets too thick; season lightly, remembering the prosciutto is salty.
Cook the fettuccine in salted boiling water 3 to 5 minutes until al dente, drain and return to the pot over medium heat.
Divide the noodles between plates, spoon over the sauce and top with Parmesan, prosciutto and walnuts; scatter with basil and serve at once.

title: "Best Ever" Moussaka
ingredients: 1 teaspoon fines herbes (see page 36) or dried oregano
method: Slice the eggplants lengthwise ¼ inch thick, salt with 1 teaspoon and leave on paper towels 30 minutes; rinse, dry and roast on an oiled sheet at 375°F for 30 minutes.
Brown the lamb with the onions and garlic over medium-high heat, crumbling it; drain in a strainer and blot on paper towels.
Return the meat to the cleaned pan with the remaining salt, pepper, nutmeg, cinnamon, fines herbes, parsley and tomato paste; add the wine and simmer 10 minutes.
Grease a 9-by-13-inch dish and dust with the bread crumbs, holding back 3 tablespoons.
For the sauce, melt the butter, whisk in the flour, then stir in the milk, nutmeg and salt until thick.
Temper the egg yolk with a little hot sauce, add the reserved crumbs, and blend back into the sauce.
Layer eggplant, meat and plenty of feta; repeat, then top with the sauce.
Sprinkle with Parmesan and bake at 350°F for 50 to 60 minutes until golden. Cut in squares and garnish with parsley.

title: Coq au Zin
ingredients: 4½ pounds chicken breasts, thighs, and legs
⅓ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
½ cup pitted, sliced Spanish green olives
1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 1 tablespoon cold water
method: Rinse and dry the chicken and dust all over with the salt, pepper and 2 tablespoons of the flour.
Cook the pancetta in the butter in a large pot over medium heat 5 to 6 minutes, then brown the chicken in batches about 5 minutes a side; set on paper towels.
Brown the remaining tablespoon of flour in the pot 1 to 2 minutes, then cook the onions, mushrooms, garlic and herbs 5 minutes.
Add the wine, tomatoes, tomato paste, stock and chicken; boil, then cover and simmer 30 minutes.
Add the pearl onions and olives and cook 10 minutes more. Lift out the chicken and keep warm under foil.
Stir the cornstarch slurry and mustard into the liquid and boil hard 6 to 7 minutes to thicken; season.
Serve the chicken in bowls with plenty of sauce and parsley, with rice or pasta and garlic bread.

title: Clove-Infused Pork–Black Bean Stew with Tomatillo–Roasted Red Pepper Salsa
ingredients: ½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
2 pounds cubed pork stew meat (from the shoulder or roast)
2 stalks celery, ends trimmed and diced
1 large red bell pepper, cored, seeded, and chopped
2 tablespoons chopped fresh oregano (1 tablespoon dried)
12 ounces tomatillos, husked, rinsed, and cut into quarters
1 roasted red pepper, seeded and chopped (see page 116)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Soak the beans 8 hours or overnight (or boil and stand 1 hour in the hot water); drain, rinse and pick over.
Toss the pork in the chili powder, cumin, cayenne, achiote, basil, pepper and salt.
Cook the pancetta in a heavy pot until barely browned; remove it and pour off the fat.
Heat the oil and sauté the pork, garlic, onion, celery, red pepper, jalapeños and oregano 7 to 8 minutes until the pork colours.
Return the pancetta and add the wine, stock, beans, cilantro, bay leaf and cloves; boil, then cover and simmer 1 hour.
For the salsa, sauté the tomatillos, onion, shallot, garlic, jalapeño, roasted pepper and cumin in the oil 10 to 12 minutes until softening; cool, then stir in the cilantro and season.
Ladle the stew into bowls, top with salsa and a dollop of sour cream, and add cilantro sprigs; serve with garlic bread or corn tortillas.

title: Grilled Lamb with Roasted Garlic–Mint Sauce
ingredients: 1½ tablespoons chopped fresh oregano (¾ tablespoon dried)
⅛ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
½ leg of lamb, boned, butterflied, and trimmed of most fat (about 2 pounds meat)
1 large whole head of garlic, unpeeled
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Mix the marinade, seal it with the lamb in a plastic bag and refrigerate at least 2 to 3 hours, turning now and then. Pat the lamb dry.
Trim the tip off the garlic head, drizzle with the oil, season, wrap loosely in foil and roast at 350°F for 45 to 50 minutes; squeeze out the cloves.
For the sauce, soften the shallots in the oil 2 to 3 minutes, add the wine and reduce by half.
Add the stock, mint, roasted garlic and mustard and reduce by half again; season.
Grill the lamb over a hot fire 8 to 9 minutes a side for medium-rare, taking the thin end pieces off first.
Slice, spoon over the sauce and scatter with mint.

title: Grilled Flank Steak with Roasted Corn–Pancetta Salsa
ingredients: ⅛ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1 rehydrated dried chipotle pepper, stemmed and minced, or ¼ teaspoon chipotle chiles in adobo (see page 175)
4 ears fresh (or frozen) corn, husks removed
½ cup chopped roasted red bell pepper (see page 116)
2 tablespoons chopped fresh basil (1 tablespoon dried)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Whisk the marinade, bag it with the steak and refrigerate 4 to 5 hours, turning occasionally; drain, keeping the marinade for basting.
Rub the corn with olive oil and roast at 350°F for 45 minutes, then cut off the kernels (about 2 cups).
Cook the pancetta over low-medium heat 8 to 10 minutes until lightly browned; drain and blot.
Mix the corn with the pancetta, bell pepper, garlic, Worcestershire, jalapeños, vinegar and basil; season and chill, then bring to room temperature.
Grill the steak over a hot fire 5 minutes a side for rare, rest 5 minutes under foil and slice thinly against the grain on an angle.
Spoon salsa onto each plate and top with slices of steak.

title: Penne with Sausage, Porcini and Portobello Mushrooms, and Syrah
ingredients: 12 ounces Italian sausage, cut into ½-inch slices
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper or red pepper flakes
1 pound dried penne or other small dried pasta
GARNISH: shredded Asiago cheese, chopped parsley
method: Soak the porcini in hot water 2 to 3 hours and drain.
Brown the sausage slices in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat 6 to 7 minutes; blot on paper towels.
In a large pan cook the onions and garlic 4 to 5 minutes until translucent, then add both mushrooms, the herbs, salt and pepper for 3 to 4 minutes.
Pour in the Syrah, boil, then simmer until reduced by half.
Add the tomatoes and tomato paste and simmer 8 to 10 minutes; return the sausage to heat through and season.
Boil the penne in salted water until al dente, drain, and toss with the sauce in the pot, reheating if needed.
Serve in four bowls topped with Asiago and parsley.

title: Grilled Lamb with Olive Sauce
ingredients: ¼ teaspoon fresh ground black pepper
1 6- to 7-pound whole leg of lamb, boned, butterflied, and trimmed of excess fat (about 4½ pounds meat)
1 tablespoon chopped fresh rosemary (½ tablespoon dried)
¼ cup pitted, sliced green olives
¼ cup pitted and sliced Kalamata olives
method: Whisk the marinade ingredients in a non-reactive bowl, pour into a large sealable bag with the lamb and marinate 4 to 6 hours, turning occasionally.
Sauté the shallots and mushrooms in the olive oil over medium heat 3 to 4 minutes, add the wine and boil down by half.
Add the stock and rosemary and reduce by half again.
Stir in the mustard and olives and simmer gently until the sauce coats a wooden spoon; keep warm.
Pat the lamb dry, keeping the marinade for basting, and grill over very hot coals 7 to 8 minutes a side to medium-rare, basting now and then; take the thin ends off early.
Rest under foil a few minutes, slice thinly and serve on warm plates with the sauce and rosemary sprigs; roasted potato quarters and tomatoes gratinée go well.

title: Filet Mignon "Diana"
ingredients: ¾ tablespoon whole mixed peppercorns, lightly crushed
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
method: Oil the filets, press the crushed peppercorns and salt onto the tops and sides, and spread the tops with mustard.
Soften the garlic in the butter over low-medium heat 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the wine, vinegar, mustard, Worcestershire, stock, Cognac and tomato paste; boil, then simmer until reduced by half.
Add the cream and reduce a little more to thicken; season and adjust the consistency.
Grill the filets over very hot coals 8 to 10 minutes, turn and give them 5 to 6 minutes more for rare, or longer to taste.
Pool the sauce on the plates and set the filets on top; asparagus and sweet potato purée suit it.

title: Roast Pork with Holy Mole Sauce and Mexican Rice
ingredients: ½ teaspoon coriander seed, toasted and crushed
1½ tablespoons chopped, seeded pasilla chiles (see NOTE)
1 tablespoon chopped chipotle chiles in adobo (see NOTE)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
8 ounces feta cheese (tomato-basil, if available), cut into ¼-inch cubes
